Subject: Operational controls questionnaire — initial clarifications

Hi Ava,

Thanks for submitting the initial questionnaire. Our audit group had a few follow-ups specifically around model serving controls, disaster recovery expectations for inference traffic, and the audit trail for customer-specific keys and API access. Main asks below: 

1) Can you confirm how long request/response logs are retained in hosted deployments by default and what the options are for customer retention windows?
2) For Private (VPC) deployments, what evidence do you provide that cryptographic keys are handled exclusively by customer KMS/HSM?
3) For DR exercises, what is your typical RTO/RPO for a dedicated pool failure, and can you share a recent runbook excerpt showing failover steps?
4) Auditability: do you provide tamper-evident logs and a chain-of-custody for config changes to model routing policies?

We are aiming to lock the controls appendix by 11/05. If you can get clarifications and any supporting artifacts (SOC2 summary, runbook excerpt) that would be ideal.

Regards,
Emily Carter
Senior Vendor Risk Manager
Bank of Oceania

(Attachment: BoO_Operational_Controls_Form.xlsx)

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Operational controls questionnaire — initial clarifications

Hi Emily —

Thanks for the detailed questions. I'm pulling together a concise package to answer each point and will include the SOC2 summary and a redacted runbook excerpt. Quick answers inline so you have context while we assemble docs: 

1) Logging retention (hosted): default 30 days for full request/response traces; configurable up to 2 years on paid plans. Customers can elect to ship logs to their own S3/GCS for arbitrary retention.
2) Private (VPC): we support customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS, and Vault). Encryption keys for model artifacts and request encryption are never exported to Redwood-managed key stores when customer-managed KMS is configured. We can supply architecture diagrams and a sample key policy.
3) DR / RTO/RPO (dedicated pool): typical recovery target is RTO <= 5 minutes for active HA pools with automatic failover; RPO depends on KV cache durability setting — usually <30s for persistent cache sync. For single-pool failover to standby region, documented exercised RTO has been ~12–18 minutes in most recent drills. We will attach an anonymized runbook excerpt.
4) Auditability: we maintain immutable append-only event logs (WAL-style) for control-plane changes with HMAC-based integrity checks and chained sequence numbers; these are available as part of our audit package and are exportable to customer SIEM.

I'll circulate the formal package by Monday EOD. If Perry (cc'd) has a specific evidence format they prefer, let me know.

Best,
Ava Chen
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

All —

Uploading the runbook excerpt. Key excerpts below (redacted): 

- Step 1: Detect degraded serving node (health checks + latency spike).
- Step 2: Auto-drain traffic from affected worker pool; control-plane writes failover intent to append-only event log (seq: 000842) and pushes alert to PagerDuty.
- Step 3: Promote standby pool in target region; warm KV cache restored from cold snapshot (approx 45s) then incrementally replay recent deltas from durable log (RPO ~ 30s).
- Step 4: Reroute DNS and update routing policy; smoke tests and synthetic traffic validation for 3 minutes before marking healthy.

Observed drill (09/18/2026): total measured failover time = 14 minutes (detection->healthy on standby). Cause: intentional node degradation test; no customer data exposure.

I've attached anonymized runbook_export_20261101.pdf and the excerpt log lines (redacted). PTAL.

-Markus
Director, Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference

- SOC2_Type_II_summary.pdf (independent auditor summary, redacted)

Short answers: 
• Logging retention: Hosted defaults to 30 days; configurable to 2 years. Customers can export to own object store for indefinite retention.
• Key custody: For Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS/HSM; keys remain under customer control and policies (we provide sample IAM/KMS policy artifacts).
• DR targets: Active HA pools target RTO <=5m; measured cross-region failover in our Sep 2026 drill was 14m. RPO depends on KV durability but typically <30s when persistent cache is enabled.
• Auditability: Control-plane events are recorded in an append-only event store with chained HMACs; we provide exports and signed digests for evidence.
